MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:41 PM CDT 4 min read
MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA) mined 2,422 bitcoin in the second quarter, a little more than it mined a year earlier. Yet revenue fell 27% to $174.9 million because the average price of each coin it produced was far lower.
That gap explains why the company wants to stop being known as a bitcoin miner. It now describes itself as an owner of power-ready land and electricity, and it hopes to rent that capacity to AI companies. But mining still pays the bills and no AI customer has signed on yet, so the question is whether a customer arrives before the bitcoin cushion thins.
MARA runs 19 data centers, most filled with machines that earn bitcoin by processing transactions, and it holds a large stash of the coin. It wants to turn some sites into data centers that rent computing space to AI customers. On the evidence so far, it is a bitcoin miner paying for an AI transition that has no customer yet. Investors who want more stocks like this can find MARA in our recent list, 9 Best Bitcoin Stocks to Buy Now.
MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
The company's reported results still move with bitcoin's price. MARA posted a net loss of $611.3 million in the second quarter, and $343.0 million of that came from marking its bitcoin down to market value. It is a paper loss, but it landed on the line investors read as profit. Mining itself kept growing, with more machines running than a year earlier even as each coin was worth less.
Sales grew about 190.9% a year over the past five years, a long record of growth. But over the past 12 months MARA lost $3.46 billion on $804.22 million in sales, so the growth never reached profit. If you own the shares, you own a bet on bitcoin's price and a bet on AI demand at the same time.
Management's answer is power. MARA is waiting on regulatory approval for Long Ridge, a power plant with more than 70% of its output sold under long-term contracts. Management expects it to add earnings once it closes. MARA also secured rights to a powered land site in Matagorda County, Texas, and together the two would lift its power portfolio to as much as 4.8 gigawatts.
No customer has signed yet. Management told shareholders it is confident of signing at least one lease before year-end, working with its partner Starwood. For investors looking to add AI power exposure, our list of 10 Best AI Energy Stocks to Buy in 2026 covers more names.
The company took on $600.0 million of new bitcoin-backed loans to help fund Long Ridge, and it bought no bitcoin in the quarter while its holdings fell 29% to 35,577 coins. If no tenant signs, the company will have borrowed against the asset that protects it.
The plan survives this, because the power assets are lined up and the lease timeline is management's own. It does limit how much credit the company deserves until a contract exists.
Because MARA loses money, the usual earnings test does not apply. The forward P/E, which divides a stock's price by expected earnings, shows no meaningful value for the company, so the stock is not priced on earnings at all. Companies in its sector carry a median forward P/E of 21.01, which shows what investors pay for expected earnings, and MARA has none to compare.
Among hedge funds, holders of MARA numbered 27 in the second quarter of 2026, up from 25 in the first quarter. The count comes from quarterly filings, so it shows professional interest edging up even though the company still loses money. If you're looking for lower-priced stocks that hedge funds hold, check out 10 Best US Stocks to Buy Under $20: Ranked by Hedge Funds.
On the other side, short interest stands at 29.84% of shares outstanding, which means traders have borrowed and sold a large share of the stock, betting the price will fall. A reading that high shows many traders doubt the story will deliver.
So the puzzle at the start has a plain answer. MARA mined more bitcoin and still reported less revenue because its results follow bitcoin's price, and the AI plan has not changed that yet. The stock is priced on that plan, which makes the lease management expects before year-end the thing to watch.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MARA as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Cryptocurrency mining stocks are brushing off a fresh round of analyst price target cuts, and buyers are stepping back in after a sharp selloff. MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction) stock is rising 4% to $7.65 this afternoon. Similarly, Hut 8 (NASDAQ:HUT) shares are up 4% to $70.61, keeping pace with MARA stock.
Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT) stock is lagging both peers, up by only 0.5% to $14.04. Piper Sandler cut its price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares in the same note, so the gains in MARA and Hut 8 shares show buyers treating the cuts as largely priced in.
Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) is up 0.7% to $82,519 over a 24-hour window, well behind the rally in MARA or Hut 8 shares. That gap suggests MARA and Hut 8 shares are rallying more on their own rebound than on any lift from the cryptocurrency.
Piper Sandler Trims Targets on Rate and Credit Worries
In a new note, Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley cut price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares, citing hotter inflation and higher oil prices that revived rate-hike concerns. Moley also pointed to credit markets repricing the debt that funds data center buildouts, along with uncertainty over planned AI capital spending. Each of those factors points straight at the financing behind data center plans at MARA, Riot and Hut 8.
Piper Sandler still maintained that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after their recent selloff, and the firm kept an Overweight rating on MARA stock. Trading in MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares initially turned lower after the note before reversing higher.
Cantor Fitzgerald had already cut its price targets on Riot and Hut 8 shares on October 16, so Piper Sandler’s note adds to a string of recent reductions for both names. Hut 8 stock is rallying through both rounds of cuts, while Riot stock is barely moving.
Power Sites Tie Miners to Bitcoin and Borrowing Costs
MARA, Riot and Hut 8 began as Bitcoin miners and are adding AI and high-performance computing data center businesses at existing power sites. That shift ties MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares to both the Bitcoin price and the cost of financing data center construction, which is also why the power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the expansion keep showing up in our free AI infrastructure report. Higher rates and repriced credit can lift the cost of each new build, which is why Moley’s concerns land directly on this corner of the market.
The CoinShares Bitcoin Mining and Digital Power ETF (NASDAQ:WGMI) is up 1% to $31.95. For broad-market context, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $768.63, a much smaller move than the mining fund. Both funds trail MARA and Hut 8 shares, while Riot shares sit below the mining ETF’s gain.
Data Center Debt Is the Next Hurdle for MARA
Another hurdle for MARA is whether credit markets keep repricing data center debt. Hotter inflation, higher oil prices and renewed rate-hike concerns all feed into that financing cost. Traders can watch for whether Riot stock joins the rebound in MARA and Hut 8 stock.
Piper Sandler’s Overweight rating on MARA stock and its view that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after the selloff give buyers a reason for confidence. Piper Sandler’s lower price targets still argue for patience. Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until the data center financing picture resolves.

MARA Holdings Sends $81M to Galaxy—What Next?
MARA Holdings sent 996 BTC worth $81.13 million to Galaxy Digital, raising questions about a sale as the US miner expands into AI.
By Maxwell MutumaOctober 9, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
MARA Holdings transferred 996.105 BTC worth approximately $81.13 million to Galaxy Digital.
Blockchain records have not confirmed whether Galaxy Digital sold the transferred Bitcoin.
MARA sold 23,093 BTC for approximately $1.6 billion during the first half of 2026.
The company’s Bitcoin holdings stood at 35,577 BTC on June 30, down from 53,822 BTC at the end of 2025.
MARA is expanding into AI and high-performance computing while managing its Bitcoin treasury and debt obligations.
MARA Holdings transferred 996 Bitcoin, valued at $81.13 million, to a wallet linked to Galaxy Digital, according to blockchain tracker Lookonchain. The October 9 movement follows months of Bitcoin sales by the miner. However, available records do not establish whether Galaxy Digital sold the coins.
Transfer Raises Questions About Bitcoin Sale
Lookonchain identified the sending address as MARA Miner and the receiving address as Galaxy Digital. The transaction involved 996.105 BTC. Galaxy Digital offers trading and custody services, so a transfer to its wallets does not necessarily represent a sale.
It seems that Bitcoin mining company MARA Holdings (@MARA) also dumped 996 $BTC($81.13M).https://t.co/fTOd8FQMxR pic.twitter.com/xr6Bk1km4N
— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) October 9, 2026
Neither company had explained the purpose of this movement in the reports reviewed. The transfer represented about 2.8% of MARA’s 35,577 BTC holdings reported for June 30, although that balance may have changed since then.
MARA held 53,822 BTC at the end of 2025, compared with 35,577 BTC on June 30. Recent data on Bitcoin miner selling pressure showed fewer extreme outflows across the wider mining sector.
MARA Holdings sold 23,093 BTC during the first six months of 2026, raising approximately $1.6 billion. Its filing said these sales helped fund operations, manage cash needs and support future investments.
The company used $912.8 million to buy back about $1 billion in convertible debt. Its June holdings also included 4,742 BTC lent to third parties and 4,528 BTC pledged as loan collateral.
Bitcoin recovered above $82,000 on Friday after declining during the week. Separately, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $484.9 million in withdrawals on October 7. Those figures describe broader market conditions, not the purpose of MARA’s transaction.
MARA Holdings stock gained about 2% before Friday’s opening bell, approaching $10. The share movement followed Bitcoin’s rebound, although the transfer has not been tied to any confirmed sale.
AI Expansion Remains a Corporate Priority
MARA Holdings is increasing its focus on artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Second-quarter revenue fell 27% to $174.9 million, while the company recorded a $611.3 million net loss.
The strategy comes amid expanding demand for AI data centers and computing infrastructure, with new construction and technical hiring accompanying industry investment. MARA has identified digital infrastructure as its primary growth focus.
For now, the latest wallet movement adds to its record of active Bitcoin management. The company has not disclosed whether these particular coins supported trading, custody, or financing activity.

Bitcoin News: MARA Sent 1,000 BTC to Exchanges as Saylor Hints at Another Buy. Is the Biggest Miner Selling?
The largest Bitcoin miner just moved 1,000 BTC onto exchanges while its holdings have quietly shrunk by thousands of coins, and now Michael Saylor is hinting at a buy. Whether that signals a sale, a loan, or something else changes…
Published October 19, 2026, 5:51am ET · 4 min read
The Crypto Desk desk. Editor: Sam Daodu.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
This conceptual image illustrates the intricate process of Bitcoin mining and its connection to the broader cryptocurrency network, reflecting the activities of companies like MARA. © thodonal88 / Shutterstock.com
MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction), the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miner, transferred 1,000 Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), valued at around $82.8 million, to the Binance and Gate exchanges over five days, according to the on-chain tracker Lookonchain. MARA hasn’t explained these transfers. So, is MARA selling Bitcoin?
In contrast, Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ:MSTR), signaled more Bitcoin purchases. He tweeted, “We found room for more orange,” his usual hint at another purchase. Strategy Inc. holds 848,250 BTC and last reported buying 250 BTC, though it has not made a new announcement yet.
Bitcoin trades at approximately $82,720. MARA shares were at $7.70 premarket, up 2.3% from the previous close of $7.53, even though they remain down 20.2% for the week and 30.3% for the month.
Meanwhile, Strategy Inc. was trading at around $140 premarket, down 9.6% for the week, as investors worry that a stock index could drop the company.
MARA’s Mining Revenue Falls as Its Costs Climb
MARA primarily earns revenue through Bitcoin mining, where specialized computers compete to add new blocks to the network and earn newly mined coins. Its revenue decreased to $174.9 million in the second quarter, down from $238.5 million the previous year. A 28% drop in Bitcoin’s average price cut revenue by $65.9 million.
MARA’s hashrate, the total computing power its machines contribute to the network, rose to 70.3 exahashes per second. However, the cost of energy needed to mine each Bitcoin has increased to $38,690 from $33,735 a year ago. Management attributed this rise to increased mining difficulty, which occurs when more machines come online.
About $343 million of MARA’s $611.3 million net loss came from a mark-to-market loss, which is a paper loss from valuing its Bitcoin at lower prices without selling any coins. Management noted that every $10,000 change in Bitcoin’s price affects that line by approximately $350 million. MARA ended the quarter with $421.3 million in cash.
MARA Is Spending Heavily on Power and AI
MARA is also moving into energy and is acquiring Long Ridge Energy, a gas-fired power plant, in a $1.5 billion deal, including debt. MARA plans to assume about $900 million of Long Ridge’s debt, and the deal is pending approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
MARA has also secured rights to a 2 GW-powered site in Matagorda County, Texas, with plans to convert most of its capacity for AI and high-performance computing through a joint venture with Starwood. Its Exaion unit already operates an AI cloud in Europe, ensuring customer data complies with European regulations. We also cover seven suppliers benefiting from similar shifts in a free AI infrastructure report.
To finance these ventures, MARA borrowed $600 million using Bitcoin-backed credit facilities with Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) and Two Prime at an average interest rate of 7.6%. Lenders can claim the pledged Bitcoin if MARA fails to repay, and the new loans left 54% of MARA’s Bitcoin pledged as collateral.
Management has indicated that MARA will continue to sell Bitcoin selectively to fund operations. Its filings support this, showing MARA held 35,577 BTC at the end of June, down from 49,951 BTC a year earlier, with no updated figures released since its August 6 earnings call.
Saylor’s Buy Hint Cannot Offset MARA’s Exchange Deposits
Companies that send coins to an exchange are often preparing to sell, as exchanges facilitate trades between buyers and sellers. However, companies also move coins for other reasons, like lending them out, using them as collateral, or hedging against price fluctuations. MARA does engage in lending; in the second quarter, it had 4,742 BTC out on loan, generating about $4.3 million in interest.
While the deposits may imply a sale, they don’t prove one. MARA reported Coinbase and Two Prime as lenders for the new credit lines, yet the coins were sent to Binance and Gate. MARA has not disclosed any specific buyers, sale prices, or proceeds, and it hasn’t confirmed the wallet labels Lookonchain assigned.
Saylor’s tweet also warrants close examination. As the head of the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, he promotes the asset central to his company’s balance sheet, but his post mentions no specific amounts, dates, or funding sources. Strategy Inc. has also sold Bitcoin this year, with $218.4 million sold to date under its Bitcoin monetization program as of its second-quarter report.
During the same period as Strategy Inc.’s last 250 BTC purchase, the company also spent $192.4 million buying back preferred shares instead of buying more Bitcoin. MARA’s deposit of 1,000 BTC is four times that 250 BTC buy.
Is MARA Selling Bitcoin? What Does It Mean for Prices?
Signs suggest MARA may be selling, or preparing to sell, some of its Bitcoin. The coins went to trading platforms, and MARA has said it sells Bitcoin selectively. It also has a power plant deal, AI expansion plans, and rising mining costs to fund. Selling Bitcoin can generate cash without diluting shareholders, but it may weigh slightly on Bitcoin prices since the proceeds go into infrastructure.
MARA’s next update should settle it. If the report shows fewer than 35,577 BTC and mentions any sales, the coins were sold; steady holdings, with more coins lent or pledged, would suggest a collateral move. An 8-K filing showing Strategy Inc. buying more than 1,000 BTC would mean one buyer absorbed the miner’s coins. MARA’s shares could still rise on FERC approval or new leases, even if Bitcoin prices stall.

MARA Has Lost 64% in a Year: Piper Sandler Sees 53% Upside ©WiR_Pixs from pixabay, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
MARA Holdings has lost 64% of its value in a year, and Piper Sandler cut its target to $11 from $13 today while keeping its Overweight rating.
The $11 target is roughly 53% above this morning's price and sits near the bottom of a Street range that runs from $10 to $30.
A lower bitcoin price led to a $611.3 million second-quarter loss, and investors are still waiting for the AI data center lease management expects by year-end.
The numbers support Piper's call, but it depends on bitcoin and on MARA signing its first lease.
MARA Holdings (MARA:NASDAQ) has lost 64% of its value over the past year (through Monday's close), and Piper Sandler just cut its price target for the third time in 2026. Even so, the firm's new $11 target sits 53% above this morning's price.
MARA's second quarter shows the problem well. Revenue fell 27% from $227.2 million a year earlier to $174.9 million as bitcoin's average price dropped 28%, and the company lost $611.3 million, about $343 million of it from marking bitcoin to market.
Management's answer is the AI pivot. On the Aug. 6 call, CEO Fred Thiel said MARA remains "confident in our ability to sign at least 2 leases before year-end."
No lease has been announced yet, and the clock on that year-end promise is running. Then October got rough for the whole group, as hotter inflation data and worries about debt-funded AI build-outs hit the miners. MARA went from $11.33 at the end of September to $7.38 at Monday's close.
Piper still says buy, just at a lower price
Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley stuck with his Overweight rating today but lowered his target to $11 from $13, his third cut this year after trimming it to $16 in January and to $13 in July.
Does $11 add up?
The rest of the Street has been lowering its sights too. The analysts' average target has slipped from $23.32 a year ago to $18.61 now, while the stock fell much further…
MARA (MARA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
That leaves Piper's $11 near the bottom of a range that runs from $10 to $30. Nine analysts rate the stock Buy or Outperform, against one Underperform and one Sell. And $11 is roughly where MARA traded three weeks ago: it closed at $11.33 on Sept. 30.
Revenue estimates are less friendly. Analysts expect $707 million this year, down from $907 million in 2025, then $805 million in 2027 and just $606 million in 2028…
MARA (MARA): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)
A signed lease is the most likely thing to lift those numbers.
On TIKR's normalized estimates, MARA trades at just over 4x forward earnings, and Piper's target implies 6.3x. The few analysts who publish GAAP forecasts still expect losses in 2026 and 2027, though smaller ones than a month ago.
A modest target, with a bitcoin-sized risk
The risk is the balance sheet. After $600 million of new bitcoin-backed borrowing, 54% of MARA's bitcoin is pledged as collateral. MARA also expects to take on about $900 million of debt when its $1.5 billion Long Ridge acquisition closes.
My take: the numbers support Piper's call. It only asks for a return to September's price at a single-digit multiple, while loss estimates are shrinking.
The test is the leases. If the first one lands before Dec. 31, along with FERC's approval of the Long Ridge deal, $11 starts to look conservative. If the year ends without one, expect more target cuts.

That gap explains why the company wants to stop being known as a bitcoin miner. It now describes itself as an owner of power-ready land and electricity, and it hopes to rent that capacity to AI companies. But mining still pays the bills and no AI customer has signed on yet, so the question is whether a customer arrives before the bitcoin cushion thins.
MARA runs 19 data centers, most filled with machines that earn bitcoin by processing transactions, and it holds a large stash of the coin. The company's reported results still move with bitcoin's price. Management's answer is power. MARA is waiting on regulatory approval for Long Ridge, a power plant with more than 70% of its output sold under long-term contracts. The company took on $600.0 million of new bitcoin-backed loans to help fund Long Ridge, and it bought no bitcoin in the quarter while its holdings fell 29% to 35,577 coins. If no tenant signs, the company will have borrowed against the asset that protects it.
The plan survives this, because the power assets are lined up and the lease timeline is management's own. It does limit how much credit the company deserves until a contract exists.

So the puzzle at the start has a plain answer. MARA mined more bitcoin and still reported less revenue because its results follow bitcoin's price, and the AI plan has not changed that yet. The stock is priced on that plan, which makes the lease management expects before year-end the thing to watch.

MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction), the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miner, transferred 1,000 Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), valued at around $82.8 million, to the Binance and Gate exchanges over five days, according to the on-chain tracker Lookonchain. MARA hasn’t explained these transfers. So, is MARA selling Bitcoin?
In contrast, Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ:MSTR), signaled more Bitcoin purchases. He tweeted, “We found room for more orange,” his usual hint at another purchase. Strategy Inc. holds 848,250 BTC and last reported buying 250 BTC, though it has not made a new announcement yet.
Bitcoin trades at approximately $82,720. MARA shares were at $7.70 premarket, up 2.3% from the previous close of $7.53, even though they remain down 20.2% for the week and 30.3% for the month.
Meanwhile, Strategy Inc. was trading at around $140 premarket, down 9.6% for the week, as investors worry that a stock index could drop the company.
MARA’s Mining Revenue Falls as Its Costs Climb
MARA primarily earns revenue through Bitcoin mining, where specialized computers compete to add new blocks to the network and earn newly mined coins. Its revenue decreased to $174.9 million in the second quarter, down from $238.5 million the previous year. A 28% drop in Bitcoin’s average price cut revenue by $65.9 million.
MARA’s hashrate, the total computing power its machines contribute to the network, rose to 70.3 exahashes per second. However, the cost of energy needed to mine each Bitcoin has increased to $38,690 from $33,735 a year ago. Management attributed this rise to increased mining difficulty, which occurs when more machines come online.
About $343 million of MARA’s $611.3 million net loss came from a mark-to-market loss, which is a paper loss from valuing its Bitcoin at lower prices without selling any coins. Management noted that every $10,000 change in Bitcoin’s price affects that line by approximately $350 million. MARA ended the quarter with $421.3 million in cash.
MARA Is Spending Heavily on Power and AI
MARA is also moving into energy and is acquiring Long Ridge Energy, a gas-fired power plant, in a $1.5 billion deal, including debt. MARA plans to assume about $900 million of Long Ridge’s debt, and the deal is pending approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
MARA has also secured rights to a 2 GW-powered site in Matagorda County, Texas, with plans to convert most of its capacity for AI and high-performance computing through a joint venture with Starwood. Its Exaion unit already operates an AI cloud in Europe, ensuring customer data complies with European regulations. We also cover seven suppliers benefiting from similar shifts in a free AI infrastructure report.
To finance these ventures, MARA borrowed $600 million using Bitcoin-backed credit facilities with Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) and Two Prime at an average interest rate of 7.6%. Lenders can claim the pledged Bitcoin if MARA fails to repay, and the new loans left 54% of MARA’s Bitcoin pledged as collateral.
Management has indicated that MARA will continue to sell Bitcoin selectively to fund operations. Its filings support this, showing MARA held 35,577 BTC at the end of June, down from 49,951 BTC a year earlier, with no updated figures released since its August 6 earnings call.
Saylor’s Buy Hint Cannot Offset MARA’s Exchange Deposits
Companies that send coins to an exchange are often preparing to sell, as exchanges facilitate trades between buyers and sellers. However, companies also move coins for other reasons, like lending them out, using them as collateral, or hedging against price fluctuations. MARA does engage in lending; in the second quarter, it had 4,742 BTC out on loan, generating about $4.3 million in interest.
While the deposits may imply a sale, they don’t prove one. MARA reported Coinbase and Two Prime as lenders for the new credit lines, yet the coins were sent to Binance and Gate. MARA has not disclosed any specific buyers, sale prices, or proceeds, and it hasn’t confirmed the wallet labels Lookonchain assigned.
Saylor’s tweet also warrants close examination. As the head of the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, he promotes the asset central to his company’s balance sheet, but his post mentions no specific amounts, dates, or funding sources. Strategy Inc. has also sold Bitcoin this year, with $218.4 million sold to date under its Bitcoin monetization program as of its second-quarter report.
During the same period as Strategy Inc.’s last 250 BTC purchase, the company also spent $192.4 million buying back preferred shares instead of buying more Bitcoin. MARA’s deposit of 1,000 BTC is four times that 250 BTC buy.
Is MARA Selling Bitcoin? What Does It Mean for Prices?
Signs suggest MARA may be selling, or preparing to sell, some of its Bitcoin. The coins went to trading platforms, and MARA has said it sells Bitcoin selectively. It also has a power plant deal, AI expansion plans, and rising mining costs to fund. Selling Bitcoin can generate cash without diluting shareholders, but it may weigh slightly on Bitcoin prices since the proceeds go into infrastructure.
MARA’s next update should settle it. If the report shows fewer than 35,577 BTC and mentions any sales, the coins were sold; steady holdings, with more coins lent or pledged, would suggest a collateral move. An 8-K filing showing Strategy Inc. buying more than 1,000 BTC would mean one buyer absorbed the miner’s coins. MARA’s shares could still rise on FERC approval or new leases, even if Bitcoin prices stall.
